rows.title: Runs programs on this machine
rows.plain_text: The agent can run the allowed programs inside the chosen folders. A program can do anything those folders allow.
rows.mitigation: Keep folders and command prefixes narrow; the OS sandbox enforces the folders.

rows.title: Changes your files
rows.plain_text: The agent can create, edit, move and delete files in the chosen folders.
rows.mitigation: Edits are hash-checked and atomic; use version control in those folders.

rows.title: Reads your files
rows.plain_text: The agent can read every file in the chosen folders, including any keys or notes stored there.
rows.mitigation: Pick the smallest folder that works.

rows.title: Data can leave via that site
rows.plain_text: A wildcard or broad host lets the agent send data to any site behind it. The allowlist does not inspect encrypted traffic, so domain fronting can escape it.
rows.mitigation: List exact hosts instead of wildcards.

rows.title: Reaches the listed websites
rows.plain_text: Sandboxed commands can talk to the listed hosts, so data can be sent there.
rows.mitigation: Only list hosts the task needs.

rows.title: Can read and change any file you can
rows.plain_text: Commands run as your own account with no sandbox: they can read and change any file your account can, including other projects and keys.
rows.mitigation: Use short durations; revoke as soon as the task ends.

rows.title: Unrestricted network
rows.plain_text: There is no network allowlist without the sandbox, so data can be sent anywhere.
rows.mitigation: Prefer workspace-write with listed hosts.

rows.title: Can leave things running
rows.plain_text: Without a sandbox a command can install things or start background programs that keep running after the grant ends.
rows.mitigation: Review running processes after the task.

rows.title: Stays until you revoke it
rows.plain_text: This access does not end by itself.
rows.mitigation: Prefer task-length access; the header chip reminds you while it is live.

rows.title: Keeps a program running
rows.plain_text: The agent can keep a program running and type into it while the lease is held.
rows.mitigation: Leases expire unless the agent keeps renewing them; you can kill it from the machine page.

rows.title: Sees everything on screen
rows.plain_text: The agent sees everything on the chosen screens, including passwords and messages.
rows.mitigation: Close private windows first. Screenshots are not stored unless you turn retention on.

rows.title: Acts as you in those apps
rows.plain_text: Mouse and keyboard input acts as you in the named apps. It is not sandboxed.
rows.mitigation: Name only the apps needed; press the stop hotkey or Stop on the overlay at any time.

rows.title: Moves your windows
rows.plain_text: The agent can focus, move and resize windows of the named apps.
rows.mitigation: Limit to the named apps.

rows.title: A launched app can open others
rows.plain_text: Apps the agent opens can themselves open other programs (browsers, editors, terminals).
rows.mitigation: Name exact apps and arguments.

rows.title: X11 has no OS permission prompt
rows.plain_text: On X11 any program can see the screen and send input; this grant is the only gate.
rows.mitigation: Prefer a Wayland session where the desktop asks you first.

rows.title: Input to any app
rows.plain_text: Input is allowed into every app, including terminals and settings.
rows.mitigation: Only possible with the unsandboxed policy on; name apps instead.

rows.title: This path is your Windows drive
rows.plain_text: Paths under /mnt inside WSL reach your Windows files.
rows.mitigation: Use paths inside the Linux home instead.

rows.title: Docker group is root-level
rows.plain_text: Adding your user to the docker group grants root-level privileges on this machine.
rows.mitigation: Prefer rootless Docker or Podman.

rows.title: Published ports bypass the firewall
rows.plain_text: Ports published by Docker Engine bypass ufw/firewalld rules.
rows.mitigation: Publish ports on 127.0.0.1 only.

rows.title: A VM uses RAM and disk
rows.plain_text: Docker Desktop and Podman machine run a small Linux VM that uses memory and disk while running.
rows.mitigation: Stop it when not needed.

rows.title: Container runtimes can mount your files
rows.plain_text: Running docker or podman lets the agent start containers that can mount folders it can reach.
rows.mitigation: Keep this grant task-length; containers are rootless by default here.
